claims.text: The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and the relevant equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets can be prepared as thermomechanically processed, single-phase FCC samples.
The alloys should be compared using identical thermomechanical processing, tensile-testing conditions, strain rate, and environment.
Variations in binary enthalpic interactions among constituent elements produce differences in local chemical ordering.
Local chemical ordering produces nanoscale compositional clusters.
Local chemical ordering raises activation barriers governing dislocation motion.
Local chemical ordering increases lattice friction through nanoscale detrapping of dislocation segments.
Differences in local chemical ordering modulate alloy yield strength.
Differences in local chemical ordering modulate work-hardening behavior.
The lower-component ternary and quaternary subsets have more pronounced local chemical order than the quinary alloy.
The stronger local chemical order in the lower-component subsets is caused by stronger pairwise enthalpic interactions.
Mn disrupts or dilutes ordering interactions in the quinary alloy.
The quinary alloy consequently has weaker local chemical order and lower barriers to dislocation motion.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have higher yield strengths.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will exhibit more pronounced work hardening.
Variations in stacking-fault energetics can alter dislocation pathways and therefore confound attribution of mechanical differences solely to local chemical order.
Grain-size differences or residual stresses may also affect dislocation behavior and mechanical properties.
Local chemical order can be quantified using microscopy, atom-probe analysis, pair correlations, or short-range-order parameters and compared with yield strength and work-hardening rate.
Failure of strength and work hardening to correlate with enhanced local-order metrics in lower-component alloys would falsify local chemical ordering as the primary driver.

contradictions.description: The prediction is stated for unspecified quaternary and ternary subsets generally, but the mechanism treats Mn as the additional constituent that distinguishes the quinary alloy. Some subsets can themselves contain Mn, and different subsets omit different elements, so the Mn-specific explanation does not consistently cover the full comparison set.
